verse: Now faith is the assurance of what we hope for and the certainty of what we do not see.
story: The writer of Hebrews has told weary believers to hold on, and now he stops to say what holding on actually looks like.

Faith, he says, is the assurance of what we hope for and the conviction of what we cannot see. It is not wishful thinking or a leap in the dark. It is settled confidence in what God has promised, and that confidence treats the unseen as real. The chapter goes on to show it in people: Abel, Noah, Abraham, who obeyed a word before they saw anything happen. Faith rests on the character of the One who spoke, and so it can stand firm before the promise arrives.
What has God promised that you cannot yet see? Trust Him with it today, as the ancients did.
